chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara and Fuzayl, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
The ritual bath (ghusl) in the month of Ramadan is at the time of the sun's setting, shortly before it. Then one prays, then breaks the fast.
ai.seo_question: When should one perform ghusl during Ramadan according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies the precise moment for the Ramadan ghusl, linking it to the sighting of the sun at sunset (maghrib) rather than the entry of night, thereby ensuring the fast is validly broken. The sequence of bathing, praying, and then eating highlights the ritual purity required before engaging in the evening meal, reflecting the Shia emphasis on aligning physical purification with the specific temporal markers of the fast.
